newsitem.title: CHINA: China reports record grain purchase amid shipment.
newsitem.headline: China reports record grain purchase amid shipment.

text.p: China has reported record state grain purchasing for the 1996 season and will transport more grains, mainly corn, from major growing areas to other parts of the country to ease stockpiles, officials said on Monday.
China is also considering corn exports to the international market if prices are favourable, an official of the State Grain Reserve Administration told Reuters by telephone.
"It's impossible for China to ban exports completely," he said. "But the exports are unlikely to be in a large amount."
He declined to give details, but traders say China may already have concluded sales of as much as two million tonnes this year. China exported 70,000 tonnes in the first two months.

China's state purchase of grains from farmers for the 1996 season hit a record 118.5 million tonnes at the end of March, up by 24.1 million tonnes compared with the year-ago period, the reserve administration official said.
The state was buying more grain in the 1996 year because of two consecutive record harvests, he said.
"The state grain purchase for 1996 is successful and almost over," the official said. "But that has created storage difficulties in producing areas because of outdated facilities."
A high proportion of damp grain could rot when the weather becomes warmer, he said, but gave no figures.
State grain reserves in northeastern Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning provinces and Inner Mongolia hit 63.1 million tonnes by end-March, up 77 percent year-on-year, the Futures Herald said.
Of the grain reserves, mainly corn, damp grain accounted for 30.15 million tonnes, the newspaper said.
Grain officials worked round-the-clock to dry out the grain and most had been dried out, it said.
To ease the pressure of mounting stockpiles, the central government has since last year ordered several shipments of corn from producing provinces to the high-consuming south.

China's northeastern provinces shipped two million tonnes of corn to southern provinces in late 1996 and a further 1.5 million tonnes early this year. A third batch of 3.0 million tonnes was now being moved.
A total of 8.7 million tonnes of grain, mainly corn, was expected to be moved by the end of June, the newspaper said.
However, domestic corn prices in the producing provinces were continuing to fall despite the shipments, officials said.
"Corn prices are still declining," an official of the Heilongjiang provincial government said by telephone from Harbin, the capital, but did not give details.

The average corn price stood at 1,170 yuan ($141) per tonne at the end of March, down 30 yuan from the end of February, the China Grains, Oils and Feeds newsletter said in an edition seen in Beijing on Monday.
